get.description: Returns every (username, IP) pair currently locked out by brute-force detection, with its consecutive failure count. Requires `manage-users` role.

get.description: Finds a stage across all of the realm's flows and returns it, including the alias of the owning flow. Requires `view-realm` or `manage-realm` role.

delete.description: Removes the stage from its owning flow. Built-in flows are read-only. The post-delete flow set is validated before persisting. Requires `manage-realm` role.

400.description: Owning flow is built-in or the post-delete set is invalid

get.description: Returns the stage's embedded authenticator configuration. Requires `view-realm` or `manage-realm` role.

404.description: Realm, execution, or configuration not found

put.description: Replaces the stage's existing authenticator configuration. Requires `manage-realm` role.

404.description: Realm, execution, or configuration not found

post.description: Attaches an authenticator configuration to the stage; a stage carries at most one. Requires `manage-realm` role.

400.description: Configuration already exists or owning flow is built-in

delete.description: Removes the stage's authenticator configuration. Requires `manage-realm` role.

404.description: Realm, execution, or configuration not found

get.description: Returns all authentication and authorization flows configured in the realm. Requires `view-realm` or `manage-realm` role.

post.description: Creates a new flow. The realm's post-mutation flow set is validated first; a 400 listing every problem is returned and nothing is persisted on failure. Requires `manage-realm` role.

409.description: A flow with this alias already exists

get.description: Returns a single authentication flow with its stages. Requires `view-realm` or `manage-realm` role.

put.description: Replaces the flow's provider id, top-level flag, and stages. The path alias wins (flows cannot be renamed via PUT), built-in status never changes, and omitted fields keep their stored values. Built-in flows are read-only. The post-mutation flow set is validated before persisting. Requires `manage-realm` role.

400.description: Built-in flow or invalid flow definition

delete.description: Deletes a flow. Built-in flows cannot be deleted, nor flows referenced by a realm flow binding (browser/direct-grant/reset-credentials/first-broker-login/registration) or by another flow as a sub-flow. The post-delete flow set is validated before persisting. Requires `manage-realm` role.

400.description: Flow is built-in, bound, referenced as a sub-flow, or the post-delete set is invalid

post.description: Creates a deep copy of the flow under a new alias: stages are cloned with fresh stage ids, the copy is never built-in, and the top-level flag is preserved. This is how a built-in flow becomes editable. Requires `manage-realm` role.

parameters.name: flow_alias
parameters.description: Alias of the flow to copy

requestBody.description: Copy request with the new flow alias

400.description: Invalid new alias or flow definition

404.description: Realm or source flow not found

409.description: A flow with the new alias already exists

put.summary: Update an execution's requirement or priority
put.description: Updates a single stage within the flow, identified by its stage id. Omitted fields keep their stored values. The post-mutation flow set is validated before persisting. Requires `manage-realm` role.

requestBody.description: Stage id plus new requirement and/or priority

400.description: Built-in flow or invalid resulting flow set

404.description: Realm, flow, or stage not found

post.summary: Add an authenticator execution to a flow
post.description: Appends a stage running the given authenticator provider at the next priority. Unknown providers are rejected by flow-set validation. Requires `manage-realm` role.

400.description: Built-in flow, invalid provider, or invalid resulting flow set

post.summary: Add a sub-flow execution to a flow
post.description: Creates a new non-top-level flow and appends a stage referencing it to the parent flow. Requires `manage-realm` role.

requestBody.description: New sub-flow alias and optional requirement

400.description: Built-in parent flow, invalid alias, or invalid resulting flow set

404.description: Realm or parent flow not found

409.description: A flow with the sub-flow alias already exists

get.description: Returns metadata about active and passive cryptographic keys (algorithms, kids, status). Requires `view-realm` or `manage-realm` role.

post.description: Generates a new active signing key and demotes the other active keys OF THE SAME ALGORITHM (rotation keeps exactly one active key per algorithm, so realms pinned to other algorithms via their `default_signature_algorithm` attribute keep their signing key). The optional body selects the algorithm and RSA key size; both default to the newest active key's parameters (the server-default algorithm EdDSA when no key exists). On an EMPTY key set the rotation establishes the fresh-deployment pair — the requested key plus, unless it is RS256 itself, an active RS256 key — so the OIDC Core mandatory-to-implement RS256 is advertised in discovery from the start. The endpoint reloads this node's keystore and returns the resulting key metadata. Signing keys are server-global (shared by all realms and cluster nodes via the `signing_keys` table); the realm path segment is namespace parity with Keycloak only. Peer cluster nodes pick the rotation up via JWKS polling. Requires `manage-realm` role.

requestBody.description: Optional algorithm/size for the new key

post.description: Imports users, groups, clients, roles, and identity providers from a realm-partial document. `ifResourceExists` (query parameter, or the same field in the body) selects the conflict strategy: `FAIL` (default) stops at the first already-existing resource with 409 naming it — resources imported before the conflict stay imported, there is no transactional rollback; `SKIP` leaves existing resources untouched and imports the rest; `OVERWRITE` updates existing resources with the document's fields. Identity matching: users by username, clients by clientId, realm roles by name, client roles by (clientId, name), groups by name, identity providers by alias. Users are imported WITHOUT credentials — credential fields in the document are ignored entirely and password hashes are never accepted through this endpoint; user role/group assignments and realm default groups are not applied. Groups are imported as top-level only (`sub_groups` is rejected). Requires `manage-realm` role.

post.description: Keycloak pushes revocation to registered clients; Issuerd has no client push channel. This endpoint exists for API compatibility: it records an admin event and returns 204 without other side effects. Set `notBefore` via `PUT /admin/realms/{realm}` to revoke previously issued tokens. Requires `manage-realm` role.

clientScopes.description: Client scopes including their protocol mappers.

clients.description: All clients of the realm, secrets omitted.

groups.description: All groups of the realm (flat list, `parent_id` carries hierarchy).

users.description: All users of the realm, without credentials.

RealmExportRepresentation.description:
Full realm export returned by `POST /admin/realms/{realm}/export`: realm
fields at the top level (Keycloak-compatible where fields overlap) plus
users, clients, groups, roles, identity providers, and client scopes.

The document carries no secret material: users never include credentials,
client secrets are omitted, and identity-provider `clientSecret` config
values are masked. Groups are a flat list — hierarchy is carried by
`parent_id` (`sub_groups` is always empty).

adminEventsDetailsEnabled.description: When `true`, admin events store the request body representation.

adminEventsEnabled.description: Whether admin (audit) events are recorded for this realm.

admin_theme.description: Theme used for the admin console.

browserFlow.description: Alias of the browser login flow (default `"browser"`).

bruteForceProtected.description: Whether brute-force detection (login-failure tracking + lockout) is enabled.

defaultGroups.description: Group paths assigned to every new user on creation.

defaultLocale.description: Fallback locale used when the client does not negotiate one.

default_role.description: Name of the default realm role assigned to new users.

directGrantFlow.description: Alias of the direct grant flow (default `"direct grant"`).

display_name.description: Human-readable display name shown on login pages.

duplicateEmailsAllowed.description: Whether multiple accounts may share the same email address.

editUsernameAllowed.description: Whether users may change their own username.

enabled.description: Whether the realm is active. Defaults to `true`.

eventsEnabled.description: Whether login/user events are recorded for this realm.

eventsExpiration.description: How long events are retained, in seconds (0 = never expire).

eventsListeners.description: Event listener ids active for this realm (default `["logging"]`).

firstBrokerLoginFlow.description: Alias of the first broker login flow (default `"first broker login"`).

id.description: Unique realm identifier. Auto-generated if omitted on creation.

internationalizationEnabled.description: Whether realm-level internationalization (localized login/email) is enabled.

lockoutDurationSecs.description: Fixed lockout duration in seconds (used when the wait increment is 0).

loginWithEmailAllowed.description: Whether users may log in with their email address instead of the username.

login_theme.description: Theme used for the login UI.

maxFailureWaitSecs.description: Upper bound for the progressive lockout wait, in seconds.

maxLoginFailures.description: Number of consecutive login failures before the account+IP is locked.

notBefore.description:
Revocation cutoff: tokens issued before this Unix timestamp are
rejected (0 = no cutoff).

offline_session_idle_timeout.description: Offline session idle timeout in seconds.

otpPolicyLookAheadWindow.description: Number of future time steps accepted when verifying a TOTP code.

registrationEnabled.description: Whether self-registration is enabled for this realm.

rememberMeEnabled.description: Whether the login form offers a "remember me" checkbox.

rememberMeSessionIdleSecs.description: Idle timeout in seconds for sessions established via "remember me".

resetCredentialsFlow.description: Alias of the reset credentials flow (default `"reset credentials"`).

resetPasswordAllowed.description: Whether users may reset their own password ("forgot password").

sso_session_idle_timeout.description: SSO session idle timeout in seconds.

sso_session_max_lifespan.description: Maximum SSO session lifetime in seconds.

supportedLocales.description: Locale tags (BCP 47) this realm can render.

verifyEmailEnabled.description: Whether email verification is enforced for this realm.

waitIncrementSecs.description: Progressive lockout wait increment in seconds (0 = fixed lockout duration).

RoleName.description:
A validated role or group name.

Rules:
* non-empty
* must not contain control characters
* max 255 characters

client_role.description: Whether this is a client role (as opposed to a realm role).

composite.description: Whether this role is a composite of other roles.

composites.description: IDs of roles included in this composite.

container_id.description: ID of the realm or client that owns this role.

name.description: Role name. Must be unique within its container.

RotateKeyRequest.description:
Optional request body for `POST /admin/realms/{realm}/keys/rotate`.
Both fields default to the newest active key's parameters
(the server-default algorithm EdDSA when no key exists).

algorithm.description:
JWS algorithm of the new key (e.g. `"RS256"`, `"ES256"`, `"ES512"`,
`"EdDSA"`). Rotation keeps exactly one active key per algorithm: other
active keys of the SAME algorithm are demoted, active keys of other
algorithms keep signing for the realms pinned to them.

key_size.description:
RSA key size in bits (2048..=8192); ignored for EC/OKP algorithms.
Symmetric (HMAC) algorithms are rejected outright.

ServerInfoRepresentation.description: Aggregated server metadata containing all available enum lists.

auth_methods.description: Authentication methods used to establish sessions.

authenticators.description:
Registered authenticator providers available for flow executions —
drives the execution provider dropdown in the flow editor.

client_installations.description:
Client installation/adapter-config providers — drives the format
dropdown of the "Download adapter config" dialog. Each `id` is accepted
by `GET /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/installation/providers/{provider_id}`.

event_listeners.description:
Event listener ids that can be activated per realm; only
`logging` is built in.

identity_provider_presets.description:
Identity provider presets: config templates that prefill the IdP form
for well-known providers.

locales.description: UI locales with a built-in message bundle.

mapper_types.description:
OIDC protocol mapper types — drives the mapper-type
dropdowns on client-scope and dedicated-scope forms.

required_actions.description: Required actions that can be assigned to users.

subject_types.description:
OIDC subject identifier types (`public` / `pairwise`) —
drives the client-form subject-type dropdown.

themes.description: Available login themes (built-in plus themes directory scan).

SyncResultRepresentation.description: Result of a user federation synchronisation run.

TestSmtpConnectionRequest.description: Request body for the SMTP test-connection endpoint.

email.description: Recipient address the test email is sent to.

TokenEndpointForm.description:
Form fields of the token endpoint used by the first-party web clients
(`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`). Every field is optional; the
`grant_type` drives which ones a given grant requires.

authorization_details.description:
RFC 9396 §7 `authorization_details` echo — the details assigned to the
issued access token, set by the authorization_code and refresh_token
grants when the grant carries RAR authorization details;
skipped everywhere else.

issued_token_type.description:
RFC 8693 §2.2 `issued_token_type` — only set by the token-exchange
grant; skipped everywhere else so the other grants'
response shape is unchanged.

TotpStartResponse.description:
Response of the TOTP enrollment start endpoint: the base32 secret, the
`otpauth://` provisioning URI, and the same URI rendered as an inline SVG
QR code (generated locally — the secret never leaves the server).

UpdateCredentialLabelRequest.description:
Request body for `PUT /users/{id}/credentials/{credentialId}`:
only the user-facing label is mutable. The primary wire spelling is
Keycloak's `userLabel`; the crate-local snake_case variant is accepted as
an alias for consistency with [`CredentialRepresentation`].

id.description: Identifier of the stage to update.

UpdateMeRequest.description:
Profile update body: a field that is absent stays unchanged, an explicit
`null` clears it (first/last name and email only — username is never
cleared).

attributes.description: Custom user attributes (key → list of values).

client_roles.description: Client role names mapped by client ID.

email_verified.description: Whether the email address has been verified.

enabled.description: Whether the account is active. Defaults to `true`.

groups.description: Group IDs the user belongs to.

id.description: Unique user identifier. Auto-generated if omitted on creation.

realm_roles.description: Realm role names assigned to this user.

requiredActions.description: Required actions assigned to the user (e.g. `"UPDATE_PASSWORD"`, `"VERIFY_EMAIL"`).

username.description: Login username. Must be unique within the realm.

clients.description: Map of client IDs to authentication methods used in this session.

ip_address.description: IP address of the client that created the session.

last_access.description: Last access time as a Unix timestamp.

offline.description:
Offline session: backs an `offline_access` refresh token
and survives SSO session expiry/logout.

started.description: Session start time as a Unix timestamp.

user_id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated user.

username.description: Username used when the session was created.

credential.description: The serialized `PublicKeyCredential` produced by the browser ceremony.

label.description: Optional user-facing label ("Work laptop") stored on the credential.
